archiveTitle: Evening Brief | Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 test addendum

entries.headline: Addendum: First early access test live, second open beta begins August 29 at 01:00 Beijing time
entries.summary: Activision's test hub page and support documents confirm that the first early access test for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 began on August 22 at 02:00 Beijing time, available to PS5, Xbox Series, and PC players who pre-ordered or have a code, running until August 26 at 01:00. The second open beta, which requires no pre-order, begins August 29 at 01:00 Beijing time and will also include Switch 2. Earlier briefs did not cover the official hub page; this entry is included as an addendum.
entries.verification: Opened the official Call of Duty test hub, Activision support page, and PC Gamer's date explanation; verified eligibility, platforms, both test weekends, and Pacific times. Addendum reason: earlier searches did not reach the official test hub.
entries.timeNote: Originally scheduled for August 21 at 11:00 Pacific, converted to August 22 at 02:00 Beijing time; outside this window, included due to earlier search omission.
entries.regionLabel: Global / eligibility and store regions vary

entries.headline: Final Fantasy X 25th anniversary lottery merchandise set for September 12 release
entries.summary: Square Enix's official merchandise account announced that the 'FINAL FANTASY X 25th Anniversary Kuji' will go on sale on September 12, with prize details to be revealed later. The same day, the Final Fantasy X 25th anniversary exhibition opens in Shinjuku, Tokyo. This indicates the anniversary project continues to expand, but pricing, sales channels, and the prize lineup have not yet been announced.
entries.verification: Opened the specific Den Fami article and verified its embedded official announcement, release date, and 'details to follow'; the original X post returned an internal error on current connection, so it is not marked official.
entries.timeNote: Den Fami article published at 15:28 Japan time; its text embeds the Square Enix official goods account announcement from the same day.

entries.headline: After first session ended early due to server issues, second session reportedly resumed as scheduled
entries.summary: The first network test session for The Duskbloods ended early after many players could not log in. Men's Journal later updated that the official account confirmed the second session resumed as originally planned on August 22 at 10:00 Beijing time. GamerSky's follow-up report also stated the second session had restarted. The official test page still lists later sessions, but the current connection could not directly open that recovery announcement, so we only confirm that media report the official said it resumed, without treating server fix status as an official conclusion.
entries.verification: Opened the official test schedule, Men's Journal update, and GamerSky's specific article. Both reports state the second session resumed, but the current connection could not locate and open the original official recovery post; therefore set to unconfirmed and continue tracking.
entries.timeNote: Resumption time converted from August 21 at 22:00 Eastern; event predates this window, included as addendum because earlier briefs missed it and follow-up reports were rediscovered in this window.

entries.headline: Producer says network test sign-ups exceeded Elden Ring Nightreign's
entries.summary: FromSoftware producer Yasuhiro Kitao stated during the August 22 Famitsu special livestream that sign-ups for The Duskbloods network test exceeded those for Elden Ring Nightreign's network test, which even surprised him. He believes positive feedback after Nightreign's release may have increased players' willingness to try the new title. The comparison reflects early interest in the Switch 2 exclusive, but the official absolute sign-up numbers for both have not been disclosed.
entries.verification: Opened the specific Famitsu program page and GamerSky's article; the program page confirms Kitao attended and gave a gameplay explanation, and GamerSky records his sign-up comparison. No absolute numbers, so only the comparative relationship is reported.
entries.timeNote: GamerSky published its report at 14:14 within this window; the original livestream began on August 22 at 20:00.

entries.headline: Eighth alleged in-development clip reported, showing entertainment venue and cutscene content
entries.summary: RockstarINTEL and GamerSky both report that Cyberleek has released an eighth alleged GTA VI in-development clip, involving an entertainment venue and cutscenes. PC Gamer independently covered another gas station clip from the same leak round. The original post or clip has been deleted or could not be safely opened, and Rockstar has not confirmed its authenticity. Therefore, we only confirm that multiple media outlets reported these claims, without confirming the visual content, build source, or the so-called full game build as real, and we do not provide leaked material.
entries.verification: Opened all three specific reports; they collectively point to Cyberleek's release, but the original post is deleted or cannot be safely verified, and there is no Rockstar confirmation. Only the existence of reports is confirmed; content authenticity, build source, and specific mechanics are unverified.
entries.timeNote: GamerSky published its report at 16:39 within this window; RockstarINTEL dates the eighth clip to August 22, but the exact original release time cannot be verified, so treated as addendum.
